primary_text_note: In copyright. Wording verified against Internet Archive search-inside (openlibrary.org/search/inside) with AND-controls, plus LitCharts/GradeSaver plot and character analysis, and the AQA 8702/2 specimen mark scheme for the exam claims.

findings.claim: “AO2 (language/structure analysis) is not formally assessed in Section A”, and the key-takeaway/exam-technique lists that name only AO1, AO3 and AO4.
findings.truth: AO2 IS assessed on the AQA Paper 2 Section A modern-text essay and is worth 12 of the 30 marks — exactly as many as AO1. The split is AO1=12, AO2=12, AO3=6, plus AO4=4 for SPaG.
findings.evidence: AQA 8702/2 specimen mark scheme, p. heading: ‘Section A: Modern texts Questions 1–24 (30 marks – AO1=12, AO2=12, AO3=6)’ with ‘AO4 [4 marks]’ on each question. https://media.aqa.org.uk/resources/english/AQA-87022-SMS.PDF ; spec 8702 confirms Paper 2 carries 27.5% AO2.

findings.claim: Enoch Powell’s Rivers of Blood speech is “directly referenced in the novel”; “Meena’s father reacts furiously to Powell’s speech”; “the response to … the speech reveals that many villagers agree”; a whole practice question and several mark schemes ask students to analyse that reference.
findings.truth: Powell is never named in Anita and Me. He is legitimate AO3 context (MP for Wolverhampton South West, a few miles from Syal’s Essington), but there is no Powell scene and no reaction to the speech in the text. The moment village racism surfaces is Sam Lowbridge’s outburst at the spring fete, when part of the crowd murmurs approval.
findings.evidence: Internet Archive search-inside (openlibrary.org/search/inside): ‘Anita Rutter’+‘Enoch’ and ‘Anita Rutter’+‘Enoch Powell’ return no edition of Anita and Me; controls ‘Anita Rutter’+‘motorway’ and ‘Anita Rutter’+‘Deirdre’ do return it, and ‘Anita Rutter’+‘Macbeth’ does not. Fete scene: LitCharts/GradeSaver plot summaries.

findings.claim: The motorway built beside Tollington is “the M6” — named in prose, in two flashcards, a knowledge check stem and a practice question.
findings.truth: The novel never names the motorway. It is simply ‘the new motorway’ announced by Mr Pembridge and objected to by Sam Lowbridge at the fete. Writing ‘the M6’ in a closed-book essay asserts a detail that is not in the text.
findings.evidence: Internet Archive search-inside: ‘Tollington’+‘M6’ and ‘Anita Rutter’+‘M6’ return no Anita and Me, while ‘Anita Rutter’+‘motorway’ does.

findings.claim: Papa (Shyam Kumar) “works at a factory despite being overqualified” — repeated in prose, in a knowledge-check answer key and in flashcards.
findings.truth: Papa has an office job. Meena never learns exactly what he does; the novel refers to his day ‘at the office’. The tyre factory in the novel belongs to Roberto Rutter, Anita’s father. The underemployment point still stands — only the workplace is wrong.
findings.evidence: LitCharts character analysis, Mr Kumar (Papa): Meena ‘does not know exactly what her father’ does and he ‘never talks about’ his day at the office. https://www.litcharts.com/lit/anita-and-me/characters/mr-kumar-papa ; LitCharts character list gives Roberto Rutter as the one who ‘works at tire factory’.

findings.claim: Of Anita’s home: “her mother Deirdre is neglectful and frequently absent, her father has left, and there is no adult supervision”.
findings.truth: Anita’s father Roberto Rutter is present throughout and works at a tyre factory. It is Deirdre, the mother, who runs off with another man (Dave) about halfway through the novel, leaving Roberto to raise Anita and Tracey.
findings.evidence: LitCharts character list: ‘Roberto Rutter — Anita and Tracey’s father; works at tire factory’; ‘halfway through the novel, Deirdre runs away, leaving her two daughters … to be raised alone by their father’.

findings.claim: “When Meena recovers and returns to the village, she discovers that Anita has moved on. Anita is now involved with Sam Lowbridge”; flashcards ask whom Anita takes up with “after Meena’s accident” and which grandmother arrives “during Meena’s recovery”.
findings.truth: The order is reversed. At Sherrie’s stable Meena overhears Anita boasting that she joined Sam — now her boyfriend — in the racist attack on an Indian man. That shock is why Meena mounts Sherrie’s horse Trixie, falls and breaks her leg. Nanima arrives much earlier, after baby Sunil’s birth, and returns to India while Meena is still in hospital, shortly before Robert dies.
findings.evidence: LitCharts and GradeSaver plot summaries: Meena overhears the ‘Paki bashing’ boast at Sherrie’s farm, then ‘suddenly decides to mount Sherrie’s horse to escape … she falls and breaks her leg’; Nanima ‘departs shortly before Robert’s death’.

findings.claim: Three lines given as quotations to memorise: “I was the only Indian girl in the village”, “I wanted to be her”, “I never saw Anita’s mum cook a meal” — also reproduced as flashcard answers.
findings.truth: None of the three is Syal’s wording; they are fabricated. Verified replacements: ‘I knew I was a freak of some kind, too mouthy, clumsy and scabby to be a real Indian girl, too Indian to be a real Tollington wench’, and Anita as ‘my passport to acceptance’. The third has been turned into a plot fact rather than an invented quotation.
findings.evidence: Internet Archive search-inside: ‘only Indian girl in the village’, ‘Anita Rutter’+‘wanted to be her’ and ‘Anita Rutter’+‘cook a meal’ all return nothing; ‘too mouthy, clumsy and scabby’ returns Anita and Me — ‘I knew I was a freak of some kind, too mouthy, clumsy and scabby to be a real Indian girl, too Indian…’; ‘my passport to acceptance’ returns ‘…was outside the home, with Anita, my passport to acceptance.’

findings.evidence: AQA 8702 spec 3.2.1 lists Meera Syal, Anita and Me under Modern texts (Prose); Paper 2 Section A is one essay from a choice of two.

findings.evidence: AQA 8702 spec 3.2.1 lists Meera Syal, Anita and Me under Modern texts (Prose); Paper 2 Section A is one essay from a choice of two.

findings.claim: Every practice question carries the same band ladder, which labels two different bands ‘Top band’: ‘Top band (26-30 marks + 4 spelling/grammar)’ and, two lines later, ‘Top band (16-20): …’.
findings.truth: AQA marks this question in six levels: Level 6 = 26–30, Level 5 = 21–25, Level 4 = 16–20, Level 3 = 11–15, Level 2 = 6–10, Level 1 = 1–5. The 16–20 band is Level 4, not a second top band. The fix is a mechanical relabel of the same ladder in all 42 questions in this unit (and it is the same ladder used across the English Literature units), so it belongs in the programme-wide band-ladder pass rather than in 42 whole-string edits here. Recommend: relabel to the AQA level names in that pass.
findings.evidence: AQA 8702/2 specimen mark scheme, Section A level table: Level 6 26–30, Level 5 21–25, Level 4 16–20, Level 3 11–15, Level 2 6–10, Level 1 1–5.

findings.claim: “The novel opens with Meena outside Mr Ormerod’s shop, stealing a charity collection tin.”
findings.truth: The theft of the charity tin from Mr Ormerod’s is right, and Meena does lie about it — she blames her cousins Pinky and Baby. Sources place the tin on the shop counter rather than outside, but the difference is not mark-affecting, so no edit.
findings.evidence: LitCharts plot summary: ‘a tin can of charity money from the counter’, blamed on Baby; Susan Elkin study guide (Internet Archive search-inside): ‘Meena steals a charity tin from Mr Ormerod and pretends that Pinky and Baby…’.

summary: All 7 lessons carry at least one real error. Eight themes: a false ‘AO2 is not assessed’ claim (AO2 is 12 of 30 marks); Enoch Powell presented as a direct reference in a novel that never names him; the motorway named as ‘the M6’; Papa moved from an office to a factory; Anita’s father wrongly said to have left (it is Deirdre who goes); the accident and the Anita–Sam discovery in the wrong order; three fabricated key quotations, two replaced with verified Syal text; and all 42 practice questions labelled ‘Shakespeare Essay’. 93 edits written.
